title: Completeness of the clause-splitting chain
statement: Let $h$ be a Boolean literal, let $R$ be a finite list of Boolean literals, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $a$ assign a truth value to each variable. Suppose every variable index occurring in $h$ or $R$ is less than $n$, and the clause consisting of $h$ followed by $R$ is satisfied by $a$. Then there is an assignment $a'$ agreeing with $a$ on every index below $n$ such that the CNF formula produced by the clause-splitting chain starting at $h$, with remainder $R$ and cursor $n$, is satisfied by $a'$.
hypotheses_covered: all variable indices in $h$ and $R$ are below $n$
the clause $h$ followed by $R$ is satisfied by $a$
replaced:
Let a clause (head plus remaining literals) have all variable indices below $n$,
and let $a$ be an assignment satisfying it. Then there is an assignment $a'$
agreeing with $a$ on all indices below $n$ that satisfies the formula emitted by
the chain construction at cursor $n$.
